title: Argo CD / Operations
description: Curated day-to-day view of Argo CD in the homelab: are all platform apps synced and healthy, are syncs failing, is the controller keeping up, is the helmfile plugin rendering, is git reachable. Built from the Argo CD v3.6.1 metrics documentation and the official dashboard (https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/blob/v3.6.1/examples/dashboard.json). The full official dashboard is 'Argo CD / Official'.

list.name: Syncs
list.textFormat: Argo CD sync of {{name}} finished with phase {{phase}}

panels.title: How to read this dashboard
panels.description: Reading guide for this dashboard.

options.content:
**What Argo CD does here.** Argo CD (namespace `argo`) deploys *everything* in the lab from the `main` branch of
this repository: the ApplicationSet `platform` creates one Application per app in `helm-charts/`, and the repo-server
renders each one with the **helmfile CMP plugin** (sidecar `helmfile-plugin`). Git is polled every 15–25 s (no webhook).
Auto-sync + self-heal are on, so *what is on `main` is what runs*.

**Healthy looks like:** every app `Synced` + `Healthy`, 0 sync failures, 0 render errors, workqueues near 0, cluster
`Connected`, git p95 well under a few seconds.

**When something is red:**
* *Out of sync / not healthy* → open the app in the Argo CD UI (`https://argocd.<domain>`), read the conditions; a
  render error (ComparisonError) usually means a broken template — run `scripts/render-app.sh <app>` locally.
* *Sync failures* → the sync result in the UI shows the failing resource (often a CRD not yet installed or an
  admission webhook rejecting the object; Argo CD retries).
* *Render errors / render latency* → `kubectl --context k8s01 -n argo logs deploy/argo-cd-repo-server -c helmfile-plugin`.
* *Controller memory near limit* → it was OOMKilled at 1 GiB with ~20 apps; the limit is 3 GiB in
  `helm-charts/argo/argo-cd/values.yaml.gotmpl`.

Alerts in this repo: `ArgoAppNotSynced`, `ArgoAppUnhealthy` (15 min). Annotations: firing alerts and restarts in `argo`, and
every finished sync (blue).

panels.title: Active alerts for this service
panels.description: Prometheus alerts of this service that are FIRING (condition true for longer than the rule's `for`) or PENDING (condition true, waiting for `for`). Same filter as the red alert annotations of this dashboard; Watchdog/InfoInhibitor are excluded. Empty = healthy. Alertmanager has no receiver in this lab, so dashboards are where alerts are seen: the rule, its threshold and source are in the rule files (helm-charts/<app>/**/prometheus.rules.yaml or the -raw release) and in docs/dashboards/. All alerts of the lab: dashboard "Alerts overview" (Observability folder).

panels.title: Applications
panels.description: Number of Argo CD Applications known to the controller (one per app of the ApplicationSet `platform` plus the root app `argo-cd`). A sudden drop means the ApplicationSet deleted apps. Source: https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/blob/v3.6.1/examples/dashboard.json.

panels.title: Out of sync
panels.description: Applications whose live state differs from git (`sync_status` != Synced). With auto-sync this should return to 0 within a minute; a value that stays above 0 for 15 min fires `ArgoAppNotSynced`. Source: helm-charts/argo/argo-cd/values.yaml.gotmpl (controller.metrics.rules); https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/blob/v3.6.1/examples/dashboard.json.

panels.title: Not healthy
panels.description: Applications whose health is not Healthy/Progressing (Degraded, Missing, Suspended, Unknown). Same condition as the alert `ArgoAppUnhealthy` (fires after 15 min). Source: helm-charts/argo/argo-cd/values.yaml.gotmpl (controller.metrics.rules).

panels.title: Progressing
panels.description: Applications still rolling out (health Progressing). Normal for a few minutes after a push; an app stuck here usually waits for a Pod that never becomes Ready. Source: https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/blob/v3.6.1/examples/dashboard.json.

panels.title: Sync failures (24h)
panels.description: Sync operations that ended in phase Error or Failed in the last 24 h. Argo CD retries automatically, so a few failures right after a push of new CRDs are expected; a steady count is not. Source: https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/blob/v3.6.1/examples/dashboard.json.

panels.title: Render errors (24h)
panels.description: Manifest generations (repo-server gRPC GenerateManifest = helmfile plugin render) that returned a non-OK gRPC code in the last 24 h. Each one is an app Argo CD could not render (ComparisonError). Source: https://github.com/grpc-ecosystem/go-grpc-middleware/tree/main/providers/prometheus. Derived query: grpc_server_handled_total counts finished RPCs by grpc_code; non-OK = failed render.

panels.title: Cluster connection
panels.description: Connection of the application controller to the Kubernetes API it deploys to (in-cluster `https://kubernetes.default.svc`). 0 = Argo CD cannot see the cluster. Source: https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/blob/v3.6.1/docs/operator-manual/metrics.md.

panels.title: Version
panels.description: Argo CD version reported by the API server (`argocd_info`). Must match the chart pin in `helm-charts/argo/helmfile.yaml.gotmpl`. Source: https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/blob/v3.6.1/docs/operator-manual/metrics.md.

panels.title: Applications
panels.description: One row per Application: sync/health status, last operation phase and auto-sync. Sorted so the problems come first is not possible in a table, so use the column filter (funnel icon) on `sync` or `health`. The `phase` column is the result of the last sync operation. Source: https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/blob/v3.6.1/docs/operator-manual/metrics.md.

panels.title: Apps with error conditions
panels.description: Applications that currently carry an error condition: ComparisonError (Argo CD could not render or compare — typically a helmfile/template error), SyncError, InvalidSpecError. Empty = no errors. Pending scrape: exported only because this repo sets `controller.metrics.application.conditions` (argocd-cmd-params-cm); appears after that change is synced. Source: https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/blob/v3.6.1/docs/operator-manual/metrics.md.

panels.title: Apps by health status
panels.description: Number of Applications per health status over time — when did an app become Degraded and for how long. Source: https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/blob/v3.6.1/examples/dashboard.json.

panels.title: Apps by sync status
panels.description: Number of Applications per sync status over time. OutOfSync spikes right after a push are normal (until the next reconciliation); a plateau is not. Source: https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/blob/v3.6.1/examples/dashboard.json.

panels.title: Sync operations by app
panels.description: Finished sync operations per Application (all phases). Each push to `main` that changes an app produces one sync; self-heal also syncs when something drifts. Source: https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/blob/v3.6.1/examples/dashboard.json.

panels.title: Sync failures by app
panels.description: Sync operations that ended in Error or Failed, per Application and phase. Open the app in the UI to see which resource failed. Source: https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/blob/v3.6.1/examples/dashboard.json.

panels.title: Average sync duration by app
panels.description: Average wall time of the sync operations finished in the window, per app. A sync that suddenly takes much longer usually waits on a hook, a webhook or a slow CRD rollout. Source: https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/blob/v3.6.1/docs/operator-manual/metrics.md. Derived query: increase(argocd_app_sync_duration_seconds_total) / increase(argocd_app_sync_total) — total sync seconds divided by number of syncs.

panels.title: Reconciliation latency
panels.description: How long one reconciliation (compare git vs live) takes, p50/p95/p99 over all apps. Higher latency means slower drift detection and slower syncs; it grows with the number of apps and with slow renders. Source: https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/blob/v3.6.1/examples/dashboard.json. Derived query: histogram_quantile over argocd_app_reconcile_bucket (the official dashboard shows the same histogram as a heatmap).

panels.title: Reconciliations per second
panels.description: Reconciliation rate per app. Each app is refreshed every 15–25 s (timeout.reconciliation) plus on every watched resource change. Source: https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/blob/v3.6.1/examples/dashboard.json.

panels.title: Controller workqueues
panels.description: Items waiting in the controller workqueues (app_reconciliation_queue, app_operation_processing_queue, …) and in the ApplicationSet queue. Sustained depth > 0 means the controller cannot keep up (raise --status-processors / --operation-processors or CPU). Source: https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/blob/v3.6.1/examples/dashboard.json; https://github.com/kubernetes/component-base/blob/master/metrics/prometheus/workqueue/metrics.go.

panels.title: Workqueue wait time (p95)
panels.description: Time an item waits in a queue before a worker picks it up (p95). Seconds here translate directly into delayed syncs. Source: https://github.com/kubernetes/component-base/blob/master/metrics/prometheus/workqueue/metrics.go. Derived query: histogram_quantile(0.95) over workqueue_queue_duration_seconds_bucket.

panels.title: Pending kubectl executions
panels.description: kubectl apply/auth operations queued in the controller. Non-zero for long means syncs are waiting on the API server (or on kubectl parallelism limits). Source: https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/blob/v3.6.1/examples/dashboard.json.

panels.title: Kubernetes API responses (non-2xx)
panels.description: HTTP responses that were not 2xx for the requests Argo CD components make to the API server, by component and code. 404s are mostly normal (Argo CD checks whether objects exist); 409 = conflict, 403 = RBAC, 422 = invalid object, 429/5xx = API server overloaded. Source: https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/blob/v3.6.1/docs/operator-manual/metrics.md.

panels.title: Kubernetes API latency (p95)
panels.description: p95 latency of Argo CD's requests to the API server, by verb. If this rises together with reconciliation latency, the API server/etcd is the bottleneck. Source: https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/blob/v3.6.1/docs/operator-manual/metrics.md. Derived query: histogram_quantile(0.95) over argocd_kubectl_request_duration_seconds_bucket.

panels.title: Cluster cache
panels.description: Objects in the controller's cluster cache (left axis) and resource watch events processed per second (right axis). The cache holds every watched object of the cluster; its size drives controller memory. Source: https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/blob/v3.6.1/examples/dashboard.json.

panels.title: Manifest renders by result
panels.description: GenerateManifest calls per second by gRPC code. OK = rendered; any other code (Unknown, DeadlineExceeded, …) = the helmfile plugin failed for that app. Renders are cached per commit, so the rate is low between pushes. Source: https://github.com/grpc-ecosystem/go-grpc-middleware/tree/main/providers/prometheus; https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/blob/v3.6.1/examples/dashboard.json.

panels.title: Manifest render latency
panels.description: p50/p95 time of GenerateManifest (helmfile template through the CMP sidecar). Pending scrape: needs ARGOCD_ENABLE_GRPC_TIME_HISTOGRAM=true on the repo-server (set in this repo's values; empty until that change is synced). Source: https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/blob/v3.6.1/docs/operator-manual/metrics.md; https://github.com/grpc-ecosystem/go-grpc-middleware/tree/main/providers/prometheus. Derived query: histogram_quantile over grpc_server_handling_seconds_bucket.

panels.title: Render queue
panels.description: Requests waiting for the repository lock (left) and p95 time waiting for the manifest-generation parallelism semaphore (right). Both near 0 = the repo-server is not a bottleneck. Source: https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/blob/v3.6.1/docs/operator-manual/metrics.md.

panels.title: Git requests
panels.description: Git operations per second by type: `ls-remote` (polling the branch every 15–25 s) and `fetch` (only when a new commit appears). Source: https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/blob/v3.6.1/examples/dashboard.json.

panels.title: Git latency (p95)
panels.description: p95 duration of git ls-remote/fetch against GitHub. Spikes = GitHub or home internet slowness; changes reach the cluster later. Source: https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/blob/v3.6.1/examples/dashboard.json. Derived query: histogram_quantile(0.95) instead of the official heatmap of the same histogram.

panels.title: Git failures
panels.description: Failed git ls-remote and fetch calls (counters only appear after the first failure, hence the `or vector(0)`). Non-zero = GitHub unreachable from the lab: nothing new will deploy. Source: https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/blob/v3.6.1/docs/operator-manual/metrics.md.

panels.title: Redis cache requests
panels.description: Requests to the Argo CD Redis cache by component; failed=true means Redis was unreachable (Argo CD then re-renders and re-computes everything: slow, CPU heavy). Redis has no exporter here; these client-side metrics cover what matters. Source: https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/blob/v3.6.1/examples/dashboard.json; https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/blob/v3.6.1/docs/operator-manual/metrics.md.

panels.title: Redis latency (p95)
panels.description: p95 latency of Redis requests per component. The controller/server expose the histogram as argocd_redis_request_duration, the repo-server as argocd_redis_request_duration_seconds (both in seconds). Should stay in the low milliseconds. Source: https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/blob/v3.6.1/docs/operator-manual/metrics.md. Derived query: histogram_quantile(0.95) over both histogram names.

panels.title: API/UI errors by service
panels.description: gRPC calls to the Argo CD API server (UI, CLI, MCP server) that did not return OK, by service and code. `Unauthenticated` comes from expired UI sessions/tokens and is usually harmless; `Internal`/`Unavailable` are not. Source: https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/blob/v3.6.1/examples/dashboard.json; https://github.com/grpc-ecosystem/go-grpc-middleware/tree/main/providers/prometheus.

panels.title: Logins
panels.description: Login requests to the API server by status (Keycloak SSO and the local admin). Failures could be a broken OIDC secret or someone guessing the admin password. Source: https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/blob/v3.6.1/docs/operator-manual/metrics.md.

panels.title: ApplicationSet reconciliation
panels.description: Reconcile latency p95 of the ApplicationSet controller (left) and number of Applications it owns (right; should equal the number of apps listed in applicationset-platform.yaml). Source: https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/blob/v3.6.1/docs/operator-manual/metrics.md. Derived query: histogram_quantile(0.95) over argocd_appset_reconcile_bucket.

panels.title: Memory working set vs limit
panels.description: Memory used by each Argo CD container (solid) and its limit (dashed). The application controller was OOMKilled at 1 GiB with ~20 apps (limit now 3 GiB); the cluster cache grows with every new CRD/object. Source: https://github.com/kubernetes-monitoring/kubernetes-mixin.

panels.title: CPU usage
panels.description: CPU cores used by each Argo CD container. Render bursts (helmfile-plugin) and reconciliation (application-controller) are the main consumers. Source: https://github.com/kubernetes-monitoring/kubernetes-mixin.
